versions.short: The law sets rules for how cars and other vehicles are designed and dealt with at the end of their life, aiming to keep their materials in use for longer. New vehicles must be built so that most of their mass can be reused, recycled or recovered, and new vehicles must include a minimum share of recycled plastic, with steel and some other materials to follow later. Each vehicle will get a free digital passport holding information on its parts, materials and spare parts. Manufacturers will have to pay for collecting and treating vehicles that reach the end of their life anywhere in the EU, and owners must hand over end-of-life vehicles to authorised facilities. The rules also cover checking that a used vehicle is not end-of-life when it changes hands, restrict exports of non-roadworthy vehicles, and require countries to cooperate against illegal dismantling and export.
